official.deadline_note: International Scholars Program application due November 15 for the September 2027 intake; required admission documents and English language results due January 31, 2027; video interviews January-March 2027; results released on a rolling basis February-April 2027
official.status_note: UBC states 'Applications for the September 2027 are open'; the application opened October 5, 2026
benefits: Financial support determined by UBC's financial need assessment
Option to participate in exchange and co-op
Dedicated advising and support from International Scholars Program advisors
Membership in the International Scholars cohort of 680+ Scholars from 111+ countries since 2001
eligibility: An international student who will be studying in Canada on a Canadian study permit
Entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school; applicants for the 2027 Winter session must have graduated no earlier than June 2026
Applying for a first undergraduate degree
Able to prove a significant level of financial need with official supporting documents, with the family unable to afford a significant level of educational costs
Demonstrates superior academic achievement (all As or equivalent standard) and meets UBC's admission requirements
Meets UBC's English Language Admission Standard, or is eligible for UBC Vantage College and the Vantage One Excellence Award
Nominated by the secondary school through one nominator and one teacher referee who must be different people
requirements: All eligibility criteria must be met; UBC states there are no exceptions to the eligibility criteria
Submit the UBC Admissions application first; the award application requests confirmation of UBC application submission
Have the nominator and teacher recommendations completed and submitted a few days before November 15
Submit the completed award application by November 15 and required documents by January 31
Complete a video interview if invited, within one week
documents: Completed International Scholars Program award application
Official documents demonstrating financial need, including family gross income, expenses and family assets
Secondary school nomination by a guidance counsellor, principal or administrator
UBC admission documents and evidence of meeting UBC's English Language Admission Standard, by January 31
selection_criteria: Students from impoverished or war-torn areas who have achieved academic excellence under challenging circumstances and would be unable to attend university without significant financial assistance
Leadership potential and a strong commitment to making a positive impact in their communities
Documented financial need assessed from family gross income, expenses and assets
Superior academic achievement (all As or equivalent standard)
coverage: Need-and-merit-based financial support assessed against documented financial need; UBC publishes no dollar value for this award category
application_method: Decide on academic program and campus by mid-September
Discuss the nomination with the secondary school in late September and confirm the nominator and teacher referee
Apply to UBC in early October, then create the award application account and invite the nominator and teacher referee
Gather family financial information and complete the award application sections; submit by November 15
Submit required documents by January 31 and complete a video interview if invited
official.application_route: UBC Admissions application first, then the online award application with school nominator and teacher referee forms, submitted by November 15
official.citizenship_residency: International students who will study in Canada on a Canadian study permit
official.international_eligibility: Open only to international students on a Canadian study permit
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The following degrees are not eligible for UBC International Scholars Program awards: Bachelor of Nursing (Okanagan and Vancouver), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management, dual degrees, joint degrees between UBC Okanagan and UBC Vancouver, and joint degrees with other post-secondary institutions
official.description: The Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award recognizes outstanding international undergraduate students from impoverished or war-torn areas who have achieved academic excellence under challenging circumstances and who would be unable to attend university without significant financial assistance. Students should demonstrate leadership potential and a strong commitment to making a positive impact in their communities. It is one of four need-and-merit-based award categories in UBC's International Scholars Program; applicants do not select which award they receive.
official.program_type: Need-and-merit-based undergraduate award within UBC's International Scholars Program for students from impoverished or war-torn areas
official.english_requirement: Must meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard. Applicants who do not satisfy it for direct entry may be eligible for UBC Vantage College and the Vantage One Excellence Award. Official English language test results must reach UBC Admissions by January 31.

verification.notes: The award's former standalone URL returns HTTP 404; the award is currently described on the official International Scholars page on you.ubc.ca, which was read directly and states no dollar value for this category.

applicant_utility.summary: The Wehrung Award targets a very specific profile - academic excellence achieved from an impoverished or war-torn background where university would be impossible without major funding - and it shares one application and one nomination channel with the three other International Scholars Program categories, so you are competing on how convincingly your circumstances and record fit that narrative. The calendar is unforgiving: nominator and teacher referee forms must be in a few days before November 15, 2026, while admissions documents and English evidence trail to January 31, 2027. Because support equals your assessed financial need rather than a published amount, your documented family finances, not your essay, ultimately set the award's size.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top students from war-affected or severely impoverished regions who can document all-As level results, profound financial need, and community impact, and who can secure a school nomination.
application_readiness_checklist: Have your school confirm the nomination slot before October - each school has only two Vancouver (including Vantage) and one Okanagan nominations
Assemble income, expense and asset documents covering the whole family well before the financial section opens
Prepare your nominator and teacher referee in early October so their forms are submitted a few days before November 15
Write the four 150-250 word essays around adversity overcome, leadership and community impact, with concrete outcomes
Get English language results to UBC Admissions by January 31, 2027, treating tests as a November deadline in disguise
common_rejection_risks: Assuming you can pick the Wehrung Award specifically - the team assigns categories automatically based on eligibility
A nomination that arrives after November 15 or a referee form left incomplete, blocking submission entirely
Financial evidence covering only the applicant rather than the whole family's income, expenses and assets
Applying to an excluded degree such as Nursing or Dental Hygiene without checking the program list
Describing hardship vaguely rather than documenting it with official papers
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award equals your assessed financial need and UBC publishes no dollar figure for it, so any gap between the assessed need and actual costs - travel, visa fees, family costs, or a need assessment your documents failed to evidence - falls on you; renewability terms are not published on the official page.
document_audit: Every claim of hardship needs an official document behind it - this award's core criterion is precisely your difficult circumstances
The nomination must come from a school or a registered non-profit acting in place of a school, not a family friend or employer
Referee and nominator must be different people, and both forms must clear before you can submit
alerts: Applying to the International Scholars Program excludes you from UBC's merit-based awards - you cannot run both tracks
UBC warns that applications started shortly before the deadline are less likely to succeed
Hold off on UBC Housing until award decisions are released; the housing deadline is May 1
The award page previously existing as a standalone URL is now part of the main program page - link to the program page, not the dead URL
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One shared International Scholars Program application (admissions application first, then nomination-backed award application by November 15), with documents by January 31 and automatic category assignment by UBC.
